judgments.reason: The span 'Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery' appears literally in the coronary angiography findings and directly supports the occlusion component of the diagnosis.
The span 'Initial serum troponin I level: 0.070 ng/mL (normal range, ≤0.028 ng/mL)' appears literally in the laboratory section and supports acute myocardial infarction via elevated troponin.
The span 'ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 through V6' appears literally in the ECG findings and supports the acute MI component of the diagnosis.

The span 'Right atrium and right ventricle lay on the left side, left atrium and left ventricle lay on the right side' appears literally in the echocardiogram findings and directly supports dextrocardia with situs inversus.
The span 'Negative P waves in lead I' appears literally in the ECG findings and is a classic ECG sign of dextrocardia, supporting the dextrocardia with situs inversus component.

The span 'QRS complexes in leads V1 through V6 showing activation of ventricle in right thorax' appears literally in the ECG findings and supports dextrocardia by indicating the heart is positioned in the right thorax.
